Database migrations, Entra-authenticated sessions, API+Postgres tenant isolation (dual-sourced: a raw-SQL RLS probe and a live API-level proof), candidate-bound audit persistence (cryptographic hash-chain verified) and Azure Monitor/OpenTelemetry evidence, and the rollback plan stage all now PASS from real deployed evidence gathered this session. Three concrete, precisely-diagnosed issues remain and keep this STAGING_NO_GO rather than fabricating a pass: (1) two dashboard pages (/dashboard/union, /dashboard/messages) were found failing the required mobile no-horizontal-overflow check for the member persona, confirmed via two independent real-navigation runs -- a real frontend defect (a CSS Grid min-width:auto default preventing long data-driven values from shrinking/wrapping on mobile) and FIXED in source (merged to main, commit feaaf27eb, PR #1182; verified via 24/24 passing component tests), but that fix has not been deployed to this authorized candidate -- deploying it requires the same separate, deliberate redeploy decision as (2) below, so the live candidate still exhibits the defect; (2) the sla-watchdog worker was found genuinely broken live (HTTP 500, root-caused to a misuse of withRLSContext for a cron actor with no real session) and FIXED in source (merged to main), but that fix has not been deployed to this authorized candidate -- deploying it requires a separate, deliberate redeploy decision outside this mandate's current authorization, so the live candidate still exhibits the defect; (3) the malware-scanning dependency for document uploads (ClamAV) has its daemon refusing connections internally despite its HTTP wrapper responding -- a real, external infrastructure gap, not an application bug, and the application correctly fails closed per policy rather than silently accepting unscanned uploads. The rollback rehearsal's automated fault-injection stage also revealed that Azure Single-revision-mode does not, on its own, prevent a bad revision from briefly receiving 100% live traffic before health verification completes -- manual recovery via a same-image redeploy is proven reliable (used successfully three times this session) but the specific zero-touch automatic protection the rehearsal set out to prove is not confirmed. See per-criterion evidence below and externalBlockers for exact remediation paths.

Blocked by a confirmed real infrastructure defect, not an application bug. POST /api/documents/upload returns HTTP 503 'Malware scanner unavailable; upload blocked by policy'. Root-caused via a dedicated connectivity probe inside the same Container Apps environment: the ClamAV scanner's HTTP wrapper responds, but the actual clamd daemon inside that same container refuses connections on its internal port (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3310) -- clamd itself is not running/listening, most likely because freshclam cannot complete a virus-definition update in this network-restricted environment. The application correctly fails closed (CLAMAV_FAIL_OPEN=false, enforced unconditionally on deployed runtimes) rather than accepting an unscanned upload -- a positive, confirmed security finding -- but this blocks completing the full document lifecycle proof (repository idempotency, foreign-org download denial, signed-URL expiry and public-access-blocked were all previously verified by code/test inspection but not re-exercised live this round because the flow cannot get past upload). See externalBlockers.

Nuanced real evidence. The rollback PLAN stage (tooling/scripts/qualify-ue-v2-staging-rollback.cjs, fixed in PR #1180/commit 132b6a1d for two Azure-API representational-format false positives) now PASSES cleanly, capturing the live healthy revision/image/templateHash. Manual recovery via a same-candidate-image az containerapp update is PROVEN reliable -- used successfully three times this session (an ActivationFailed bookkeeping fix, the rehearsal incident below, and the original Priority-1 recovery pattern), each restoring full healthy service within under a minute with zero candidate drift (identical image digest and /api/version gitSha before and after every time). The automated REHEARSE stage (deliberate fault injection: a bad revision with a broken NODE_OPTIONS) revealed that this Container App's Single-revision-mode does NOT, on its own, keep live traffic on the known-good revision while the new one is unverified -- the bad revision reached 100% traffic weight while reporting healthState None, causing a real (brief) service disruption that required the manual recovery above. This is genuine operational-recovery evidence but does not support the specific zero-touch automatic-protection claim the rehearsal set out to prove. Follow-up diagnosis: the app DOES have a correctly configured Kubernetes-style readiness probe (httpGet /api/ready, port 3000, initialDelaySeconds 10, periodSeconds 10) -- this is not a missing-health-check oversight. The root cause is architectural: ingress.traffic is configured as [{latestRevision: true, weight: 100}], so traffic always follows 'whichever revision is newest' rather than being pinned to a known-good revision name during cutover; Single-revision-mode does not gate that cutover on the readiness probe passing first the way a manually-orchestrated blue/green promotion in Multiple-revision-mode would. Changing this would mean switching the app's revision mode and deployment model, a significant, standing operational change well beyond this rehearsal's scope -- not attempted unilaterally.

externalBlockers.description: The nzila-ue-v2-staging-clamav Container App's HTTP wrapper responds but its internal clamd daemon refuses connections on port 3310 (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3310), confirmed via a direct in-environment connectivity probe. Likely cause: freshclam cannot complete a virus-definition download in this network-restricted environment, or a container startup/entrypoint issue. The container emits no console logs to the shared Log Analytics workspace, preventing further diagnosis without direct container exec access. Follow-up re-confirmation: forced a fresh replica (scaled from zero) and checked it directly -- restartCount is 0 and runningState is Running (not crash-looping; the process stays up), and a live, direct console-log stream to that replica (not just the Log Analytics forwarder) also shows zero application output, ruling out a crash loop and narrowing the cause to either a silently swallowed clamd startup failure or stdout not being surfaced by this image at all. No Dockerfile or build source for this image (nzilaventuresacr.azurecr.io/ue-clamav-http-adapter) exists in this repository, so its startup sequence cannot be inspected from source either.
externalBlockers.remediation: Needs an operator with exec/shell access to the nzila-ue-v2-staging-clamav container (or its image/entrypoint source) to check clamd's own startup logs and confirm whether outbound egress to ClamAV's definition-update servers is allowed from this environment's VNet; do not work around by setting CLAMAV_FAIL_OPEN=true, which would defeat an intentional security control.
